increments.title: DR1 puts the document being added, and the button that saves it, inside a bordered group headed "File upload"; the frontend runs the whole page as one flat column so nothing shows which button acts on the row in front of the user.
increments.detail:
The upload page is a single unbroken column: heading, Document reference, Date of issue, the file field, "Save and add another", the saved-documents table, then "Continue", "Save and return to hub" and "Cancel and return to hub" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:16-92). There is no heading, border or container of any kind between them, so "Save and add another" and "Continue" read as two buttons in the same list. A user cannot see from the page that the first acts on the fields above it and the second leaves the page — which is the difference that costs them the row they have typed.

The fields, "Save and add another" and the saved-documents table sit inside a bordered section headed "File upload", labelled to the group by aria-labelledby (app/views/upload-documents.html:92-240). The page-level actions — "Save and continue", "Save and return to overview" and "Cancel and return to overview" — sit outside the border, below it (:242-260). The grouping is what tells the user which button belongs to the document in front of them and which belongs to the page, and it holds on every state of the page: dr1-upload-documents shows the empty group, dr1-upload-documents-populated shows the saved row inside the same border.

Wrap the reference, type, date and attachment fields, the "Save and add another" button and the saved-documents table in a bordered group with an h2 of "File upload", and leave the page-level save actions outside it. Use a govuk-frontend container rather than a bespoke card — the summary-card border is the closest match already in the toolbox — and reference the h2 from the group so the grouping is announced as well as drawn. No behaviour changes; this is layout and one heading.

increments.title: DR1 opens the upload page with guidance on which documents to attach — an ITAHC instruction, a list of other documents, and an expandable table of consignment-specific requirements with a link to GOV.UK; the frontend goes straight from the heading to the first form field.
increments.detail:
Under the "Upload documents" heading the page renders the Document reference input immediately (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:16-39). There is no introduction, no list of documents a trader might need, no expandable guidance and no outbound link. The page's copy file holds no guidance keys of any kind (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:1-25). A user who does not already know which documents their consignment needs is told nothing on the page where they have to decide.

Three blocks sit between the heading and the form (app/views/upload-documents.html:38-82). First an intro paragraph: "You must attach an ITAHC if this consignment requires one. If you do not have it now, you can add it later. All documents should be uploaded before the consignment arrives at the UK port. Documents must be in English and you must upload all pages." Then "Other documents you may need to attach include:" over two bullets — "import licences or authorisations" and "commercial documents or invoices". Then a collapsed details component, "Check which additional documents you must upload", holding a two-column table headed Consignment / Documents needed with three rows — animals that do not need a health certificate need an exporter's declaration that they are fit to travel; livestock transiting bluetongue restricted territories need a bluetongue declaration GBHC172; rodents imported for research purposes need an RM39 licence and a supplementary health certificate — followed by "Check the documents you need on GOV.UK (opens in a new tab)" linking out to the IPAFFS guidance page.

Add the three blocks to the upload page between the heading and the form, in DR1's order: the ITAHC intro paragraph, the "other documents you may need" bullets, and a govukDetails holding the three-row table and the GOV.UK link. All of it is static content, so it is one template and one copy-file change with no data behind it. Two things need a decision before it is written: whether the outbound link keeps DR1's analytics-tagged URL or points at the plain guidance page, and whether the three table rows are the settled content or a placeholder the content designer will replace.

increments.title: DR1 lists JPG among the file formats a document can be in; the frontend's list omits JPG even though it accepts .jpg files.
increments.detail:
The second bullet reads "a PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, PNG, XLS or XLSX" — seven formats, no JPG. A .jpg file is in fact accepted: it is in the allowed set and in the picker's accept attribute (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/upload-config.js:10-11,24-26). It disappears from the hint because the hint is built by collapsing the allowed set on MIME type and JPG shares image/jpeg with JPEG, so only the first of the pair survives (:28-36). The same collapsed list is reused verbatim in the rejection message, so a user whose file is rejected for some other reason reads a list that does not include the extension they are holding.

The second bullet reads "PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, JPG, PNG, XLS or XLSX" — eight formats, JPEG and JPG named separately (app/views/upload-documents.html:167).

List JPG alongside JPEG in the file-type hint and in the file-type rejection message. The fix is in how the hint is derived: build the label list from the allowed extensions rather than from their MIME types, so that formats sharing a MIME type are both named. The accepted set itself does not change.

increments.title: DR1 labels a saved document's virus check "Scanning for virus" and then "Check completed"; the frontend labels the same two states "Checking" and "Safe".
increments.detail:
The Status column of the saved-documents table shows a tag whose text comes from four scan states: "Checking" while the scan is pending, "Safe" when it completes, "Virus found" when it fails, "Unknown" when the status cannot be read (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:52-57, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/view-model/fragments/status.js:7-24). The captured row on fe-documents-populated reads "Safe" in a green tag. Neither shared label matches DR1's: "Checking" does not say what is being checked, and "Safe" is a verdict about the file where DR1's is a statement about the check.

The same column carries a blue "Scanning for virus" tag while the check runs and a green "Check completed" tag once it passes (app/routes.js:9077-9086). dr1-upload-documents-populated-scanning is the blue state on a row that has just been saved; dr1-upload-documents-populated is the green one. Each tag is preceded by visually hidden text, "Virus check status for {document reference}", so the column is named per row for a screen reader (app/views/upload-documents.html:217-224).

Rename the two shared status tags to DR1's wording — pending becomes "Scanning for virus", complete becomes "Check completed" — in both language copy files, and carry the change into the scan-status announcements the client bundle reads from the same copy. The frontend's two extra states, virus found and unknown, have no DR1 counterpart to align to and keep their current wording. The frontend already has both of DR1's states, so this is copy, not behaviour.

The requirements list has two bullets and neither refers to archives (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:43-48). A ZIP is refused, because the accepted set is the eight document and image extensions and nothing else (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/upload-config.js:3-18), but the user only learns that after choosing the file, from the generic type message "The selected file must be a PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, PNG, XLS or XLSX". It is on the page before the user opens the file picker, and it gives the reason rather than only the rule. It is visible on dr1-upload-documents and on every error state of the page.

Add the ZIP bullet to the requirements list under "Your file must be:", in DR1's words. This is copy only — the frontend already rejects archives, so no validation changes.

increments.title: Every task on the DR1 hub is a link a user can follow in any order; the frontend locks a row shut behind the answers that come before it and shows 'Cannot start yet'.
increments.detail:
A frontend hub row is a link only if the first page behind it passes its entry gate; when it does not, the row is rendered as plain text with the status 'Cannot start yet' and no way in (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:93-123). Those gates chain on two answers — country of origin and the commodity selection (src/server/app/bridge/obligation-source.js:30-33) — and every page that sits after them in the journey order demands them (src/server/app/flow/prerequisites.js:13-27). A user who has given their country of origin but not yet chosen a commodity comes back to the hub and finds 'Main reason for importing' and every unconditional row below it reading 'Cannot start yet' — nine of the eleven rows on the page, from the reason for import through to check and submit, are plain black text with no way in. That hub is fe-hub-no-commodity: the only two rows a user can open are the one they have already answered and the commodity picker itself. A conditional row whose questions are all out of scope is dropped from the list entirely rather than blocked (:116-118), which is why 'Exit details' is absent from that page rather than shut.

DR1's hub gives every task an href with no condition attached (app/routes.js:5734-5836) and the template renders each one as a link (app/views/notification-hub.html:60-75). There is no blocked presentation and no 'Cannot start yet' wording anywhere in DR1. A user can open the tasks in whatever order suits them and leave gaps behind.

Stop deciding whether a hub row is a link from the answers given elsewhere in the notification. Each row should link to its own first page whatever else is unanswered, which means the prerequisite chain that makes country of origin and the commodity selection preconditions for every later page has to stop applying to hub entry. Where a page genuinely cannot be filled in without an earlier answer — an identification page that needs to know which commodity, say — that has to be handled on the page itself rather than by hiding the way in. The 'Cannot start yet' status goes with the blocked presentation.

FALSIFIED BY: A frontend hub reached on a notification where the commodity has not been chosen that still renders 'Arrival details' and the rows below it as links.

increments.title: DR1 gives commodity details a hub task of its own with its own status; the frontend hides that page inside the 'What are you importing?' task, so a user cannot see or start it separately.
increments.detail:
One frontend task, 'What are you importing?', covers two pages: the commodity picker and the consignment-details page behind it (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:29-33). Its single status covers both, which is why the captured hub reads 'In progress' — the commodity is chosen but its details are not filled in. There is no separate entry point to the consignment-details page from the hub, and no separate indication of whether it is done. Confusingly, the frontend does use the words 'Commodity details' on the hub, but as the caption of group 2, which holds two different tasks.

DR1 has two tasks. 'What are you importing?' in group 1 covers choosing the commodity, and 'Commodity details' opens the consignment-details page as the first task of group 2, 'Description of the goods', with a status of its own (app/routes.js:5771-5776). A DR1 user can see at a glance that they have picked their commodity but not yet described the consignment, and can go straight to the second without passing through the first.

Split the frontend's 'What are you importing?' task in two: leave the commodity picker as task 1 in 'About the consignment', and add a 'Commodity details' task at the head of the second group pointing at the consignment-details page, with its own completeness. The frontend's group 2 caption has to change at the same time so the group is not named after one of the tasks inside it, which the group-structure finding already covers.

FALSIFIED BY: A DR1 hub where the consignment-details page is reached from the 'What are you importing?' task rather than from a task of its own.

increments.title: DR1 shows the animals and packages totals from the moment a notification is created; the frontend hides the whole summary, heading and all, until a commodity has been added.
increments.detail:
A user who has answered where the consignment comes from and not yet chosen a commodity opens the hub on the heading 'Overview' and then goes straight into '1. About the consignment'. There is no 'Your commodities' heading and no totals above it — the picture is fe-hub-no-commodity, and the string does not occur in that page at all. The heading and the two totals cards are wrapped in a condition on there being at least one commodity line (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/template.njk:8-26), and the totals are built as null when there are none (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:142-151). Add a commodity and the block appears: the same user, one answer later, meets a page with a new section at the top of it, and the cards read 0 and 0 until a number of animals is given.

DR1 renders the summary section unconditionally and shows '0' in each card until there is something to count (app/views/notification-hub.html:26-50). The captured DR1 hub is of a notification where nothing has been answered at all and it still shows 'Your commodities' with 0 animals and 0 packages/boxes. The shape of the page does not change as the notification is filled in.

Render the commodity summary on every hub, showing zero in both cards when there is nothing to count, so the page keeps the same shape from the first visit to the last. One condition removed from the template and a zero default where the totals are built.

FALSIFIED BY: A frontend hub on a notification with no commodity added that still shows the 'Your commodities' heading and its two cards.

Both frontend states are now photographed against DR1's single unchanging one, so the claim is observed rather than read, and confidence is raised from medium to high. Two details the pictures add. increments.title: The frontend hub carries an Exit details task DR1 does not have — DR1 asks where the consignment goes on to and when it leaves as part of the main reason for import.
increments.detail:
Group 1 of the frontend hub holds a fourth task, 'Exit details', hinted 'Where the consignment travels on to and when it leaves Great Britain' (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/copy/copy.en.js:39-42). It stands for three pages of its own — destination country, port of exit and exit date (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:35-39) — and it appears with its own status tag whenever the reason for import puts any of those questions in scope. It is absent from the captured hub because the captured notification has no reason for import yet. The 'Main reason for importing' task next to it covers only the reason itself and the internal-market purpose (:34).

DR1's hub has three tasks in 'About the consignment' and no exit task. Destination country, port of exit and exit date are asked on the reason-for-import page itself, as conditional reveals under the answer that calls for them, and they count towards the 'Main reason for import' task: that task reads Complete only once the reveal's own questions are answered too (app/routes.js:1343-1367). A DR1 user sees one task for the whole of why-and-where-onward, and its status covers all of it.

Fold destination country, port of exit and exit date into the 'Main reason for import' task so the hub shows three tasks in group 1, not four, and so that task's status reflects the follow-up answers as well as the reason. The dependency is the reveal change itself, owned by the origin-and-reason slice: while the three questions live on pages of their own the task row is the only thing holding them, so this cannot land first. Doing it removes the Exit details row and with it the return-route defect that row has today.

FALSIFIED BY: An 'Exit details' or equivalent fourth task appearing in DR1's 'About the consignment' section for any reason for import.

increments.title: A user importing horses temporarily cannot get back to their port of exit and exit date from the hub — the Exit details row is shown but has no link, even though both questions are compulsory.
increments.detail:
A user who has chosen temporary admission of horses, answered port of exit and saved it, and then returned to the hub, finds the 'Exit details' row sitting there as plain black text with nothing to click and the words 'Cannot start yet' beside it. The row is not hidden and not empty — it is the entry to two questions this reason makes compulsory, one of which the user has already answered. The picture is fe-hub-exit-details-blocked and the rendered row is a `<li class="govuk-task-list__item">` carrying no `<a>` at all, where every other startable row on the same page carries `govuk-task-list__item--with-link` and a link. The row stands for three pages in order — destination country, port of exit, exit date (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:35-39) — and whether it is a link is decided by the first of those alone: `rowGatePasses` tests `row.pages[0]` (src/server/app/flow/navigation.js:25). Under this reason destination country is out of scope while port of exit and exit date are both in scope and mandatory (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js:64-113), so the first page fails its gate and the whole row is shut. The status is misleading as well as the link: `blockedRowItem` throws the row's real status away and substitutes 'Cannot start yet' whatever it was (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:95,122), so a row that is genuinely in progress tells the user they cannot begin work they have already partly done. The user can still reach the two questions going forwards, because `nextInSection` walks past the out-of-scope page to the next one that passes (src/server/app/flow/navigation.js:27-37), so they can complete the notification — but once they have left those pages they cannot get back to change an answer. Two lines above the faulty gate, `rowEntry` already does the right thing: it picks the first page whose gate passes (:20-23).

The question does not arise in DR1, because DR1 has no exit-details task. Port of exit and exit date are asked inline on the reason-for-import page as a conditional reveal under the temporary-admission answer, and they count towards that page's own 'Main reason for import' task (app/routes.js:1361-1364). A DR1 user returns to them by opening 'Main reason for import' again, which is always a link.

Make `rowGatePasses` agree with `rowEntry` — a row is enterable when any of its pages passes its gate, not only the first. That is a one-line change in src/server/app/flow/navigation.js and it restores the return route for the temporary-admission case. It is worth doing on its own even though the larger change of folding these questions into the reason-for-import task would remove the row altogether, because that change is bigger and this defect is live today.

FALSIFIED BY: A hub rendered with reason for import set to temporary admission of horses that shows the 'Exit details' row as a working link.

finding.correction:
The defect is real and every step of it was re-traced at frontend 76a864ba. rowGatePasses is one line and tests row.pages[0] only (src/server/app/flow/navigation.js:25); the Exit details row's pages are destination country, port of exit, exit date in that order (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:35-39); under temporaryAdmissionHorses destinationCountry is inScope false while portOfExit and exitDate are both inScope with status mandatory (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js:66-115); pageGatePasses fails on an out-of-scope page (src/server/app/flow/gates.js:23-32), so the row renders blocked while its status is not NA and it is therefore not hidden. The narrow framing was checked and is the right one: the section named 'consignment' holds import reason, import purpose, destination country, port of exit, exit date and additional details in one list (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:48-58), nextInSection skips the pages that fail their gate (navigation.js:27-37), and Save and continue reaches it through nextTarget, whose hub fallback only fires when the user pressed the return-to-overview button (src/server/app/shared/kit.js:76-101). So the pages are reachable going forwards and unreachable on return, which is what the finding says. Two changes made: confidence dropped from high to medium, because the state is not in the corpus at all — fe-hub is the only frontend hub shot and it was captured with no reason for import, so the conditional row is hidden in it; and the frontend slot now says that outright rather than leaving a reader to assume the picture shows a blocked row. SECOND PASS, after the state was captured: fe-hub-exit-details-blocked was shot after this finding was written, and it shows the defect rather than implying it. Confidence is back to high. The capture was driven to exactly the reason this finding names — temporary admission of horses — with port of exit selected and saved and exit date left empty, and the rendered hub holds `
  • Exit details … Cannot start yet
    • ` with no anchor anywhere inside it, against `govuk-task-list__item--with-link` on the three rows above it. The falsifier was therefore put to the one test that could fire and did not fire. One thing the capture found that the finding did not say, and the frontend slot now says: the status text is not the row's own. `blockedRowItem` (hub/controller.js:95) spreads the base row and overwrites `status` with the cannot-start constant, and buildRowItem hands every gate-failing row to it (:122), so the status the row actually earned — in progress, since one of its two in-scope questions is answered and the other is not — never reaches the page. The row does not read as 'answered but inert'. It tells the user they cannot start yet, which is the opposite of true. That makes the defect worse than a missing link: it is a missing link plus a false statement about the user's own work, and whoever fixes rowGatePasses should check that the unblocked row then shows its real status.

increments.title: DR1 shows an identification task only when the chosen commodity has identifiers to give; the frontend always shows one, so a user is told to identify animals the service will not ask them about.
increments.detail:
'Animal identification details' is an unconditional task row (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:41-45): it has no conditional flag, so the hub renders it whatever commodity has been chosen, and whether or not one has been chosen at all. The captured hub is of a notification with no commodity details filled in and the row is there, reading 'Not yet started'.

Make the identification task conditional on the chosen commodity actually calling for identifiers, so it disappears from the hub when it does not apply — the hub already has the machinery for this, since the exit-details and transit-countries rows are declared conditional and drop out when their answers are out of scope. What the identification page itself should ask of a commodity with no typed identifiers is a separate finding on that page.

increments.title: DR1 ends the notification hub with a Review and submit button a user can press at any point; the frontend makes review a task row that cannot be opened until every mandatory answer is given.
increments.detail:
The frontend hub's last group is '6. Check and submit' and it holds one task row, 'Check and submit', hinted 'Check your answers before you submit the notification'. In the capture that row is plain black text with no link and the status 'Cannot start yet'. The only button on the page is a secondary 'Return to dashboard'. The row becomes a link only once the whole notification is ready: the review section is gated on `readyForCheckYourAnswers` (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:81-85), and until that passes the hub renders the row blocked (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:72-91). A user part-way through a notification therefore has no way of opening their check-answers page at all; the only thing on the hub that goes anywhere other than into a task is the button back to the dashboard.

DR1's hub has no review task and no sixth group. The task list ends and two buttons follow it: a primary 'Review and submit' going to the review page, and a secondary 'Return to dashboard' (app/views/notification-hub.html:81-92). The primary button carries no condition, and the review page it leads to has no completeness guard on it (app/routes.js:10006-10016), so a user can go and look at the review of a half-filled notification whenever they want.

Drop the 'review' row from the hub's group list, and the '6. Check and submit' group with it, and put a primary 'Review and submit' button above the existing secondary 'Return to dashboard'. The button must not be gated on completeness — gating it would reproduce exactly what the row does today — which makes the dependency the check-answers page itself: it has to render an unfinished notification rather than being closed off by the review section's `readyForCheckYourAnswers` gate. What the check-answers page then says about the parts still outstanding belongs to the review slice.

increments.title: DR1 puts each commodity's identifier boxes in the order that commodity's own list gives; the frontend puts them in one fixed order for every animal, so a cow is asked for its passport before its ear tag.
increments.detail:
The boxes come out in the same order whatever animal is being identified, because the order is a property of the service rather than of the commodity: the identification copy block declares passport, tattoo, ear tag and horse name in that sequence and the card renders whichever of them are in scope without resorting them (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/identifier/fields.js:21-30). On the captured cow the person is asked for Passport number, then Tattoo, then Ear tag number. The two free-text fallbacks are appended after the typed fields by the same rule.

DR1 asks for each commodity's identifiers in the order that commodity's own list sets, and the orders genuinely differ: cattle is Ear tag then Passport, a horse is Microchip, Passport, Horse name, and a cat, dog or ferret is Microchip, Passport, Tattoo (app/data/commodity-identifiers.js:3-19). The panel simply loops the list it is handed, so the data is the order. On the captured cattle panel the person is asked for the ear tag first — the identifier a cow actually carries — and the passport second.

Move the identifier order off the copy block and onto the commodity, so each commodity carries its identifiers as an ordered list and the card renders them in that order. Two of the frontend's commodities disagree with DR1 today: a cow should read Ear tag then Passport where it currently reads Passport then Ear tag, and a horse should read Microchip, Passport, Horse name. This has to be settled before the microchip field is added, because a global order has nowhere to put a field that DR1 asks for first on some commodities and not at all on others, and after tattoo comes off cattle, because until then the cow panel has a third box in the middle of the pair.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding DR1's cattle panel render Passport above Ear tag, or finding the frontend sort a commodity's identifier fields by anything other than the order they are declared in the copy block.

increments.title: DR1 lets a consignment of one species be submitted without a single animal identified; the frontend will not let the notification be reviewed until every animal on every line has an identification record.
increments.detail:
Identifying the animals is compulsory on every consignment, and it is compulsory animal by animal. The unit record on each commodity line carries `recordCountEquals` against that line's number of animals, so the line is not finished until it holds exactly as many identification records as animals counted, and each of those records must carry at least one identifier (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:88-103). Until that is true the 'Animal identification details' row on the hub is not complete, and because the review section is gated on every applicable row being complete (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:81-85), 'Check and submit' reads 'Cannot start yet' — which is what the captured hub shows. A trader bringing in two hundred salmon has to enter two hundred records before the service will show them their own notification.

DR1 asks for identifiers on every species that has an identifier set, but requires them for submission only when the consignment holds more than one species, and even then only one complete record per species: `requiresAnimalIdentifiersForSubmit` is multiple-species AND some-species-has-identifiers, and `hasMinimumAnimalIdentifiersForSubmit` returns true outright when that is false (app/routes.js:1511-1524). So a consignment of a single species can be submitted with nothing identified. dr1-review-notification-incomplete is that case: one species, two cattle, no identifiers entered, and the Identification details card is not marked incomplete and is not among the five entries in the error summary — the five are additional details, arrival details, transport details, roles and addresses and the contact address. `reviewSpeciesCardErrorState` returns no error at all when identifiers are not required for submit (app/routes.js:4456-4459). DR1 does not forget the gap: it carries it forward to the confirmation page as one of two soft follow-ups, 'complete the animal identifier information in the notification' (app/routes.js:5674-5692).

Stop making a complete set of identification records a precondition of reviewing and submitting. Follow DR1's rule: identifiers are required for submission only where more than one commodity line has a typed identifier set, and then only one complete record per line, not one per animal. The per-animal count rule stays as the definition of the task being finished — it is what the hub status and the identification page's counter are built on — but it stops gating the review page, and the outstanding identifiers become a follow-up on the confirmation instead. Order this after review--incomplete-notification-cannot-be-reviewed, which moves the completeness check off the page gate and onto the POST; this finding decides what that check includes. It also decides which cards can carry the per-card error state that finding builds, so the two should be picked up together.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding DR1 refuse Continue, or mark the Identification details card incomplete, on the review page of a single-species notification with no identifiers entered.

increments.title: DR1 asks for a microchip number on horses, cats, dogs and ferrets; the frontend has no microchip field anywhere in the service.
increments.detail:
A person identifying an animal is offered at most four identifier types — passport, tattoo, ear tag and horse name — and which of them appear is decided by four commodity allowlists in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:107-113. A horse, the commodity DR1 asks for a microchip first of all, is asked for two things: fe-animal-identification-horse is headed 'Horse (0101) — Equus caballus' and offers 'Passport number' and 'Horse name' and nothing else. There is no microchip field on any commodity, and no microchip obligation exists to render one: the six unit-record identifier obligations in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:113-198 are passport, tattoo, ear tag, horse name and the two free-text fallbacks.

DR1 asks for a microchip on the two identifier sets a companion animal or an equine falls into. A horse (commodity code 0101) is asked for Microchip, Passport and Horse name, and a cat, dog, ferret or other live mammal (all commodity code 01061900) is asked for Microchip, Passport and Tattoo — app/data/commodity-identifiers.js:3-19. Microchip is the first field on both panels, so it is the identifier DR1 puts in front of the person first.

Add a microchip identifier to the per-animal record: a new unit-record obligation alongside the existing five in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js, a MICROCHIP_COMMODITIES allowlist holding Horse, Cat and Dog in the stub's picker-name vocabulary, a label in the identification copy block, and the new obligation id added to the unit record's requires.anyOfIds so a microchip on its own satisfies the at-least-one-identifier rule. Adding it also widens the derived union behind specificIdentifierWhitelists, which is what stops a microchip-only commodity falling through to the free-text fallback fields.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a microchip field rendered on the frontend's horse, cat or dog identification panel, or finding that DR1's horse and 01061900 identifier sets do not include a Microchip entry.

finding.correction: The finding stands. The carried-over claim it rests on — that app/data/commodity-identifiers.js is release-agnostic, so a set written for DR2.1 also describes DR1 — was checked at the root mount and holds. The identification page resolves a species' fields through getIdentifierFieldsForSpecies (app/routes.js:1458-1471), which calls getIdentifiersForCommodityCode on the commodity's code and returns whatever that file holds; there is no release test anywhere on that path, no equivalent of the isDesignRelease21SessionData filter that getSearchCommodities applies to the commodity catalogue itself (app/routes.js:61-73), and the one release-conditional thing in the file — the germinal-product sets under 05119985 and 05111000 — is unreachable in DR1 because those commodities are never offered. Horse 0101 and companion-animal 01061900 are both in DR1's catalogue and both carry Microchip. Two things are read from source rather than seen: neither captured page holds a horse or a companion animal, so nobody has photographed a DR1 microchip field, and the claim that Microchip is 'the first field on both panels' is a reading of the template loop over the data order rather than an observation. Medium confidence is the right band, and the named control will not resolve to a crop on either captured screen. SECOND PASS, after the state was captured: a horse line was driven and shot as fe-animal-identification-horse after this finding was written, and it settles the frontend half by absence. The panel a person meets when identifying a horse holds exactly two boxes, 'Passport number' and 'Horse name', where DR1's horse set is Microchip, Passport and Horse name — so the missing field is now missing in a picture, on the one commodity in the frontend's catalogue where DR1 asks for it first. The falsifier's frontend limb was put to the only test that could fire and did not. Confidence raised to high. Two things stay true from the first pass and should not be read as settled by the capture. DR1's microchip panel is still unphotographed — neither DR1 screen holds a horse or a companion animal — so the prototype half remains a read of app/data/commodity-identifiers.js, and the claim that Microchip is the first field on both DR1 panels remains a reading of the template loop over the data order. And the named control still resolves on no captured screen at all, on either side: it is absent from the frontend by definition and absent from DR1's cattle panel by data. The crop will not render and the report will fall back to a whole-page shot of fe-animal-identification-horse, which is the right page to look at even so, because what it shows is the gap.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a microchip field rendered on the frontend's horse, cat or dog identification panel, or finding that DR1's horse and 01061900 identifier sets do not include a Microchip entry.

relatedTo.why: the same per-commodity identifier sets; both are corrections to which identifier types a commodity is asked for

increments.title: DR1 asks nothing at all about identifying a commodity that has no identifier type of its own; the frontend asks for free-text identification details and an animal description instead.
increments.detail:
Every commodity gets an identification record. Where the commodity is on none of the four identifier allowlists — of the five commodities the frontend offers, that is Fish — the record falls back to two free-text fields, 'Identification details' (hinted 'Any other way this animal is identified, if it has no passport, tattoo or ear tag') and 'Animal description'. fe-animal-identification-fish is that page: a salmon line headed 'Fish (0301) — Salmo salar', with those two boxes and no others, asking a person to say in prose how one fish out of a consignment is told from the next. The fallback obligations apply by the inverse gate at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:174-198, and the person must still enter one record per animal counted before the task can complete.

DR1 asks for identification only where the commodity has a typed identifier set. Ornamental fish carries an empty identifier list (app/data/commodities.js:281-284), so it gets no panel, and there is no free-text fallback anywhere in DR1. On a consignment where no commodity has identifiers the page does not exist for that person at all: the identification task row is dropped from the notification overview and a request for the page redirects on to additional details.

Two changes travel together and both are needed for the page to behave as DR1 does. Drop the identificationDetails and description obligations so a commodity with no typed identifier gets no fields, and make the identification page and its hub task row conditional on at least one commodity line having a typed identifier — today the page is always reachable and the unit-record count rule still demands one record per animal. Check what the at-least-one-identifier rule on the unit record means once the fallbacks are gone: a fish line would have no identifier obligation able to satisfy it.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a free-text identification or description field rendered on any DR1 identification panel, or a DR1 identification panel rendered for a commodity whose identifier list is empty.

DR1: fourteen of its twenty-one commodities carry an empty identifier list, ornamental fish among them (app/data/commodities.js:280-290), and nothing in DR1 offers a free-text identifier of any kind. The claim that a direct request for the page redirects on is true and is worth pinning down, because the guard that would obviously do it does not — redirectIfNoAnimalIdentifiers (app/routes.js:1252-1254) returns false and is never called. The redirect is inside the renderer instead: renderAnimalIdentificationDetailsPage returns res.redirect('/additional-animal-details') when hasAnimalIdentifiersRequired is false (app/routes.js:8893-8897), which covers both the GET and every re-render after a post. The dropped task row is at app/routes.js:5777-5781 and the dropped journey step at :1265-1267. Two notes on scope rather than truth. The difference slot opens 'Two changes travel together' and the second of them — making the hub task row conditional — is already its own finding, hub--identification-task-always-shown, which says in as many words that what the page should ask of such a commodity is left to this one. The two overlap and a dependency link is added; whoever schedules them should take the hub row from that finding and the page's fields and redirect from this one. That half rests on ornamental fish carrying an empty identifier list in app/data/commodities.js and on the redirect inside renderAnimalIdentificationDetailsPage, both re-read in the first pass.

increments.title: The identification page's green button reads 'Save and finish' where every other page in both services reads 'Save and continue', and DR1 reads 'Save and continue' here too.
increments.detail:
At the foot of the identification page the green button reads 'Save and finish' — the only page in the service where it does not read 'Save and continue'. Every other journey page takes the shared macro's default (src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:5); this page passes an override at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/animal-identification.njk:25, using the string at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:95. The button behaves like every other Save and continue: it saves whatever is in the open record and moves the person to the next page.

DR1's identification page ends with 'Save and continue', the same words as the rest of its journey, and does the same thing — it captures the open record for any single-animal species and moves on (app/views/animal-identification-details.html:144-148, handled at app/routes.js:10415-10423). DR1 keeps 'Save and finish' for a different job entirely: it is the in-panel button on the last outstanding animal of a species, meaning finish this species, not finish this page.

Change the identification page's primary button to 'Save and continue' and let it take the shared default, in English and Welsh. Small on its own, but it stops mattering less once identification--save-and-add-another-always-shown lands: that finding puts 'Save and finish' on the in-card button for the last outstanding record, and if the page-level button still says the same words the page would show two identically labelled buttons doing different things. Doing this one first, or with it, avoids that.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding DR1's identification page ending in a button labelled anything other than 'Save and continue', or finding the frontend's 'Save and finish' does something its 'Save and continue' does not.

increments.title: DR1 treats an animal as identified only when every identifier its commodity asks for is filled in; the frontend accepts a record with any one of them.
increments.detail:
A person can save a cow with only an ear tag, leave the passport and tattoo boxes empty, and the record counts. That is what fe-animal-identification-saved shows: the saved row reads 'Animal 1 — Ear tag: UK123456789012' with no passport in it, and the page has moved the person on to 'Enter details for Bos taurus 2 of 2' rather than presenting the first animal again. Every identifier field is declared optional and the unit record requires just one of the six to be present (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:88-102); pressing Save and add another with all boxes empty is the only thing rejected, with the at-least-one-identifier message. Once one record exists per animal counted, the task reports itself complete.

DR1 counts an animal as identified only when every field on its commodity's identifier set holds a value — a cow needs both an ear tag and a passport, a horse needs a microchip, a passport and a horse name (app/routes.js:1526-1563). A partly filled record is stored but does not count: the panel presents the same animal again with the values it already has, the entry counter does not advance, and the identification task never reports complete.

Raise the per-record rule from 'at least one identifier' to 'every identifier in scope for this commodity line'. That means changing the unit record's requires from anyOfIds to a rule over the in-scope identifier obligations, and moving the individual identifier obligations from optional to mandatory so each empty box names itself in the error summary rather than the record failing as a whole. Do this after the commodity identifier sets are correct, because the rule is only as good as the set it ranges over — with tattoo still on cattle it would demand a tattoo for every cow. DR1 shows no error message when a record is incomplete, so the messages are the frontend's to author.

increments.title: The frontend refuses to save the origin page until a country of origin is chosen; DR1 lets the user save what they have and shows the task as still to do.
increments.detail:
Save and continue with no country chosen returns the page with 'Select the country where the animal originates from' in the error summary and against the field, and nothing on the page is kept. A user who knows the internal reference but is waiting on the health certificate to confirm the country cannot record what they do know (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:63-67).

DR1 saves whatever is on the origin page and moves on. Country of origin is not checked at all on submit — the only check the page makes is on the region code once Yes is chosen (app/routes.js:245-262). The unanswered country still counts against the task: the hub reads the origin task as complete only when both the country and the region-code answer are present (app/routes.js:232-244), so the gap is shown rather than enforced, and it is caught again at the review page before the declaration.

Stop blocking on country of origin at the page and let a partly answered origin page save. Keep the field mandatory for completeness, so the hub still shows the task as unfinished and the review page still stops a submission without it. The same save-what-you-have behaviour already applies on the frontend's reason-for-import page, so the pattern exists — this brings origin into line with it. Check the other pages in this slice for the same mismatch before treating it as an origin-only change.

increments.title: A user importing horses on temporary admission can leave the exit date blank and continue with no message; DR1 asks for it on the spot with 'Enter an exit date', a message the frontend does not have.
increments.detail:
Exit date is a date picker on a page of its own, reached only when the reason is Temporary admission horses. An empty box passes: the only check the page makes is that a value, if given, parses as a real date, and the only message the page owns is 'Enter a real exit date' (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/exit-date/controller.js:21, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/exit-date/copy/copy.en.js:8). There is no message for the date being missing anywhere in the service. The rule itself is not missing: the obligation model makes the exit date mandatory whenever the reason is temporaryAdmissionHorses (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js), so the Exit details hub row stays incomplete and Check your answers cannot be opened without it. The user is let past the page and stopped later, with no words to explain either.

DR1 requires the exit date once Temporary admission horses is chosen and distinguishes the two failures: an empty box gives 'Enter an exit date' and an unparseable one gives 'Enter a real date', each in the error summary and against the field (app/routes.js:1424-1432). The same submit also requires the port of exit, so a user leaving both blank sees two entries in the summary. DR1 carries the rule at the later points too — the hub reads the reason task as complete only when both are present (app/routes.js:1343-1367), and Continue on the review page is refused without them (app/routes.js:10068-10075).

Add the page-level check and the message that goes with it: reject a submit with the exit date empty when the reason is Temporary admission horses, with 'Enter an exit date' in the summary and against the field. The obligation is already mandatory under that reason, so nothing in the model moves — this is a validator and a copy string. Align the invalid-date message too: DR1 says 'Enter a real date' where the frontend says 'Enter a real exit date'; keep whichever the service settles on, but do not ship two different phrasings of the same failure across the journey.

FALSIFIED BY: Submitting DR1's reason page with Temporary admission horses chosen, the exit date empty and a port of exit selected, and reaching the next screen.

increments.title: The frontend rejects an internal reference containing a space, hyphen or slash; DR1 accepts whatever the user's own system calls the consignment.
increments.detail:
The field invites 'any internal reference you want to use to identify this consignment', but only letters, numbers and underscores get through. Typing ACME-2026/01, or a reference with a space in it, returns the page with 'Internal reference must only contain letters, numbers and underscores'. There is also a 58-character ceiling, with 'Internal reference must be 58 characters or less' (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:75-82).

DR1 asks the same optional question with the same label and the same hint, and imposes no rule on it at all: the submitted value is trimmed and stored, and no length or character check runs (app/routes.js:9240-9244). A user pastes in whatever reference their own records use.

Drop the character rule so hyphens, slashes, spaces and full stops are accepted — the whole point of the field is that it is the user's own reference and the service does not read it. Keep a length ceiling if downstream storage needs one, but say the limit in the hint rather than only in an error, and confirm 58 is a real constraint rather than an arbitrary one, because DR1 states no limit.

increments.title: The frontend offers 78 UK ports and airports as the port of exit; DR1 offers only the ten border control posts approved for animals, so a user can choose a port their consignment cannot lawfully leave from.
increments.detail:
Port of exit is a select of 78 entries drawn from the general ports-of-entry reference list — Aberdeen Harbour, Cambridge Airport, Chatham Docks and the rest — each labelled with a UN location code, and the hint says so: 'Choose where the consignment will leave Great Britain. Exit and entry share the same port list.' Nothing marks which of them can handle animals, and any of the 78 is accepted (src/server/app/services/ports/index.js:9-14, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/port-of-exit/copy/copy.en.js:5-6).

DR1 offers ten, and every one of them is a border control post designated for live animals, labelled with its BCP code: Edinburgh, Gatwick, Glasgow, three Heathrow posts, Holyhead, Manchester, Prestwick and Stansted (app/data/exit-border-control-posts.js:3-14). Anything else is rejected with 'Select a port of exit'. The same ten serve both the transit reveal and the temporary-admission reveal — DR1 uses one exit list, not one list per reason.

Restrict the port of exit to ports designated for live animals and label each with its BCP code, so the user cannot pick a port that cannot receive the consignment. The frontend does not hold that designation: the ports list it reads carries a code and a name and nothing else, so this needs the reference data service either to expose the designation or to serve an animal-BCP list of its own. Until that lands the frontend cannot filter. Drop the 'Exit and entry share the same port list' hint at the same time — DR1's exit list is not the entry list, so the sentence would be wrong.

increments.title: A user who picks Internal market can walk past the purpose question and reach the next page with no message; DR1 stops them there and then with 'Select a purpose in the internal market'.
increments.detail:
Picking Internal market sends the user to a page of its own, 'Purpose in the internal market', with eleven radios. Save and continue with none of them chosen is accepted: the empty value passes validation, the page saves and the user goes on (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/import-purpose/controller.js:25-30). Nothing on the page says the answer is needed and no message is ever shown for a missing purpose. The service does hold the rule, but only later: the obligation model makes the purpose mandatory whenever the reason is internalMarket (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js), so the reason hub row stays incomplete and Check your answers cannot be opened until the purpose is chosen. The user meets a page that accepts an empty answer and a hub that will not let them finish, with nothing joining the two up.

DR1 will not let the reason page be saved with Internal market chosen and no purpose behind it. Save and continue returns the page with 'There is a problem' and one entry, 'Select a purpose in the internal market', and the same message appears in red inside the reveal above the eleven radios, with the reveal left open and the red bar running down its edge. The summary link moves focus to the first radio (app/routes.js:1387-1394). This is the state the captured error screen shows. DR1 carries the rule at the later points too — the hub reads the reason task as complete only when the purpose is present (app/routes.js:1343-1367), and Continue on the review page is refused without it (app/routes.js:10068-10075).

Add the page-level check the frontend is missing, so the user is told at the point of the mistake instead of finding a hub row they cannot clear: reject a submit with Internal market chosen and no purpose, with 'Select a purpose in the internal market' in the summary and against the field. The obligation is already mandatory under Internal market, so this is a validator change on one page and nothing in the model moves. Where the message is shown depends on the reveal change: while purpose is a page of its own the error belongs on that page, and once it moves inline it belongs in the reveal, as DR1 shows it. Do this first — it stands on its own.

increments.title: DR1 asks the four questions that the reason for import opens inline, as reveals under the reason the user picks; the frontend asks them on four pages of their own reached through a separate hub task.
increments.detail:
The frontend asks the main reason on its own page and then, depending on the answer, sends the user on to as many as three further pages, each with its own heading, its own Save and continue and its own return to the hub. Internal market leads to 'Purpose in the internal market'. Transhipment or onward travel leads to 'Destination country'. Transit leads to 'Destination country' and then 'Port of exit', in that order. Temporary admission horses leads to 'Port of exit' and 'Exit date'. Reason and purpose sit in one hub task and the other three sit in a second, conditional task called Exit details (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:34-39). A user answering for transit therefore visits three pages and crosses two hub tasks to answer one question and its consequences.

DR1 asks all of it on one page. The radio group on 'Main reason for import' carries a conditional reveal under four of its five options (app/routes.js:8778-8820), and the questions appear in place the moment the radio is chosen: Internal market reveals the eleven-option 'Purpose in the internal market' radio group; Transhipment or onward travel reveals a Destination country select; Transit reveals Port of exit and then Destination country, in that order; Temporary admission horses reveals an Exit date picker and then a Port of exit select. Re-entry reveals nothing. One page, one Save and continue, one hub task. Every reveal is present in the rendered page and hidden until its radio is chosen, which is why the captured temporary-admission state carries all six reveal fields in its DOM.

Move the four follow-up questions onto the reason page as govukRadios conditional reveals and retire the four separate pages, in reveal order per reason: purpose under Internal market; destination country under Transhipment; port of exit then destination country under Transit; exit date then port of exit under Temporary admission horses. Both the transit pair and the temporary-admission pair come out in the reverse of the frontend's page order today. One consequence follows: the Exit details hub task disappears, and with it the trap where that task renders as a visible unlinked row under Temporary admission horses because its gate tests only the first of its three pages. DR1 has no equivalent trap because it has no second row to gate, so a reason that opens only exit date and port of exit cannot produce a dead row. That hub change is owned by the hub slice and depends on this one. Answers do not need a separate decision: both sides drop a reveal answer once its reason is no longer chosen, so nothing changes about what survives a flip.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding that DR1 routes away from /reason-for-import to a separate page for any of purpose, destination country, port of exit or exit date, rather than rendering it in the conditional block on the reason page itself.

CLAIMED (in difference): 'DR1 holds a separate stored answer per branch, so a user who picks Transit, answers, switches to Transhipment and switches back still sees the transit answers; the frontend's single destinationCountry and portOfExit fields are purged'. Every POST to /reason-for-import writes null to each branch field whose reason is not the one submitted (app/routes.js:10252-10265, and the same nulling in the soft-save branch at :10222-10241), so Transit then Transhipment then Transit loses the transit answers on DR1 too. If anything the frontend keeps MORE, not less: because one destinationCountry field serves both Transit and Transhipment, a country answered under Transit is still in scope under Transhipment and carries over, where DR1's transhipmentDestinationCountry starts empty. That carry-over is the same per-branch-naming artefact described below, not a DR1 requirement, so it is not raised as its own finding. increments.title: DR1 fills in the country half of the region of origin code for the user and asks only for the rest; the frontend asks the user to type the whole code themselves.
increments.detail:
Answering Yes to 'Does the consignment have a region of origin code?' reveals one text box labelled 'Region of origin code', hinted 'For example, FR-75' and five characters wide. The user types the country prefix, the separator and the region part into that one box, and nothing checks that the prefix matches the country they picked above. Five characters is also too short for the example the hint gives once a longer prefix is involved (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/template.njk:24-34).

DR1 reveals the same question as a prefixed input. A read-only grey prefix box, derived from the country of origin the user has already chosen, sits immediately left of a five-character text box. The label is 'Enter the region of origin code' and the hint is 'Enter up to 5 characters', which now describes only the part the user has to supply. On submit the prototype joins the two with a hyphen (app/views/partials/region-of-origin-code-input.html:1-31). Picking France shows FR, so the user types 75 and the service records FR-75.

Split the field into a country-derived prefix and a suffix input, using the same country-to-prefix mapping the country list already needs, and change the label and hint to match. Widening the input alone is not the fix: the point is that the user cannot get the prefix wrong. This depends on the country list change, because the prefix table is keyed on DR1's country labels. Keep the joined value as what is stored, so nothing downstream has to learn about two fields.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding that the region-of-origin prefix box is rendered only for a design-release-2 session, so a DR1 user types the whole code into one field as the frontend does.

increments.title: A user can answer Yes to having a region of origin code, leave the code blank and move on to the next page with no message; DR1 stops them on the page and asks for it.
increments.detail:
Choosing Yes reveals the region of origin code box, and the page does not require it. The only check the page makes on the field is that it is at most five characters long; an empty value passes, the page saves and the user goes on to the next question with a Yes on record and no code against it, with no message anywhere on the way (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:63-82). The rule is not absent from the service — it is applied late. The obligation model makes the code mandatory whenever the requirement radio is Yes (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/origin.js), so the Origin hub row stays incomplete and the Check your answers page cannot be opened at all until the code is filled in. What the user actually meets is a Yes with no code, no explanation at the point of the mistake, and a blocked hub row later.

DR1 treats the code as required the moment Yes is chosen, and says so where the mistake is made. Save and continue with the box empty returns the page with 'There is a problem' at the top and 'Enter the region of origin code' both in the summary and against the field, and the summary link moves focus into the box (app/routes.js:253-259). Answering No skips the question and nothing is asked. DR1 also carries the same rule at the two later points the frontend uses: the hub reads the origin task as complete only when the code is present under Yes (app/routes.js:231-245), and Continue on the review page is refused while it is missing (app/routes.js:10068-10075).

Add the page-level check the frontend is missing, so the message arrives when the user makes the mistake rather than as a stuck hub row later: make the region of origin code mandatory at submit whenever the requirement radio is Yes, with 'Enter the region of origin code' in the summary and against the field. This is a validator change on one page, not a model change — the obligation is already mandatory under Yes, so nothing downstream moves and nothing needs a new pattern. Leave the No branch alone.

FALSIFIED BY: Submitting DR1's origin page with Yes selected and the code box empty and reaching the next screen.

increments.title: The frontend explains the destination country, the port of exit and the exit date with guidance DR1 does not have; DR1 asks all three with a bare label, and one of the frontend's sentences will be untrue once the exit port list is corrected.
increments.detail:
Each of the three follow-up questions carries a line of grey guidance under its label. Destination country reads 'The country the consignment travels on to after Great Britain.' Port of exit reads 'Choose where the consignment will leave Great Britain. Exit and entry share the same port list.' Exit date reads 'The date the animals are expected to leave Great Britain. For example, 27/3/2026' — the example, plus a sentence of explanation in front of it (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/destination-country/copy/copy.en.js:5, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/port-of-exit/copy/copy.en.js:5, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/exit-date/copy/copy.en.js:5).

DR1 asks all three with a label and nothing else. The captured reason page carries hints on the five reason radios and on the eleven internal-market purpose radios, and exactly one field hint — 'For example, 27/3/2026' on the exit date. Neither destination-country select and neither port-of-exit select has a hint at all: the label sits straight above the control (app/views/reason-for-import.html). The reasons themselves are where DR1 puts the explanation, and by the time a reveal opens the user has already read which reason they are in.

Drop the destination-country hint and the port-of-exit hint, and cut the exit-date hint back to its example, so the three follow-up questions read as DR1 asks them. Do this with the reveal move rather than before it: once the questions sit under the reason they answer, the reason's own hint is the explanation and repeating it under the field is the duplication DR1 avoids. The port-of-exit sentence has a second reason to go — 'Exit and entry share the same port list' is a statement of fact about the current list, and it becomes untrue the moment the exit list is narrowed to animal border control posts.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a hint rendered under either destination-country select or either port-of-exit select on DR1's reason page, or a second sentence in DR1's exit-date hint.

increments.title: DR1's confirmation page tells a user who submitted an incomplete notification what they still have to do before the consignment is imported; the frontend has no such section.
increments.detail:
Below the reference panel the confirmation page shows the declaration date and then goes to 'Transporting the consignment', at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/confirmation/template.njk:4-21. There is no outstanding-items section, and nothing in the confirmation copy or controller that could produce one. The frontend does reach the state that section is for: readiness treats a task row as satisfied when it is fulfilled, not applicable or optional (src/server/app/flow/section-status.js:11-15), so a notification with no documents uploaded passes the gate. The captured Check your answers page is exactly that notification, and its user can submit with the health certificate still to come and be told nothing about it.

When the notification was submitted with things still outstanding, the page opens under the panel with 'Before the consignment is imported', the line 'You still need to:' and a list of what is left — in the capture, 'upload the health certificate and any other required documents' and 'complete the animal identifier information in the notification' (app/views/notification-submitted.html:27-37). The list is built at submission time and holds only the two things DR1 lets a user submit without: documents, which are never mandatory, and animal identifiers, which are a soft follow-up once the per-species minimum is met (app/routes.js:5674-5692). Everything else DR1 treats as mandatory and refuses to submit without, so the section never carries it.

Record, at the moment the declaration is submitted, which optional-at-submission items were left outstanding, and render them on the confirmation page under a 'Before the consignment is imported' heading with the line 'You still need to:' above a bullet list, between the reference panel and 'Transporting the consignment'. Start with the one item the frontend can already produce — no documents uploaded — because the documents task row is optional and a notification with none of them already submits today. Add the animal-identifier item alongside whatever the identification work settles about a per-species minimum. Nothing blocks this: it needs no change to what the frontend will let a user submit.

increments.title: DR1 lets a user review a half-finished notification and names every section still to be completed on the page itself; the frontend refuses to open the review page until every task is done, so an incomplete notification has no review page at all.
increments.detail:
The whole review section — Check your answers, the declaration and the confirmation — sits behind one gate: `gate: (scope) => scope.readyForCheckYourAnswers` in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:81-85, where readiness is every applicable task row being complete (src/server/app/flow/section-status.js:11). increments.title: DR1 puts an Alpha phase banner with a feedback link on every page; no page in the frontend has one.
increments.detail:
There is no phase banner anywhere in the service. Between the service name bar and the page content the user meets the breadcrumb trail and the back link and nothing else, so nothing on any page tells them the service is in alpha and nothing invites them to send feedback. The shared layout has no phase-banner block at all — src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:41-53 renders only breadcrumbs and the back link into `beforeContent` — and no feature template adds one. This is service-wide: all 33 captured frontend screens report a null phase banner in the page model.

All 40 captured DR1 screens carry it, including the dashboard, the overview, the declaration and the confirmation page. Each view renders it itself in its `beforeContent` block — app/views/origin-of-the-import.html:13-25 is the pattern every other DR1 view repeats.

increments.title: DR1's navigation bar carries Dashboard, Address book, Manage account and Log out on every page; the frontend's carries the service name and nothing else.
increments.detail:
The navigation bar under the GOV.UK header shows the service name "Import notification service" as a link home, and no navigation items at all — the bar is an empty shell on all 33 captured screens. What account actions there are sit somewhere else entirely: a small right-aligned strip below the bar showing the signed-in user's email address and a "Sign out" link (src/server/common/components/service-header/template.njk:9-29), which the layout injects at src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:34-39. So the user gets Sign out but has no way from the navigation to reach the dashboard, an address book or their account, and the strip reads as a status line rather than as navigation.

Every page carries a service navigation bar with the service name followed by four items: Dashboard, Address book, Manage account and Log out. The Dashboard item is marked active on the dashboard pages. All 40 captured DR1 screens carry the same four. The nav is authored, not inherited from the kit — app/views/layouts/main.html:104-127 builds it explicitly, and the design-release-2 branch above it adds a fifth item, which is how you can tell the item list is a per-release decision rather than a default.

Populate the service navigation in src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:27-32 with the four DR1 items and give the item labels a home in src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js under `layout`, plus the Welsh pair in copy.cy.js. Three of the four have somewhere to point today: Dashboard is the existing notifications list at `/`, Log out is the existing `/auth/sign-out`, and Manage account is a dead `#` in DR1 too so it can wait on a real destination. Address book is the exception — the frontend consumes the address-book service as data but has no page for it, so that item cannot be wired until an address-book page exists; ship it last or ship it pointing at the same placeholder DR1 uses. Once the bar carries Log out, decide what remains of the right-aligned user strip: DR1 shows no signed-in identity anywhere, so keeping the email while adding Log out to the nav would state the same action twice.

increments.title: DR1 shows the draft status and the notification reference from the first page of a new notification; the frontend withholds both until the first answer is saved.
increments.detail:
A strip carrying a blue "Draft" tag and the notification reference sits above the page heading on 29 of the 33 captured screens. Origin of the import is the one journey page without it: on a brand-new notification the page shows the heading with nothing above it, so the user starting a notification cannot see its reference until they have saved the first page. The strip is suppressed deliberately — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:88-89 passes the journey to the layout only once the notification has committed answers, and src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:65-70 renders nothing when it is absent.

DR1's origin page shows the strip unconditionally: a "Draft" tag and the reference GBN-AG-26-7K8M2P sit between the back link and the caption, exactly as they do on every later page. The view includes the shared status partial with no guard at all — app/views/origin-of-the-import.html:29 — and app/views/partials/notification-status.html:18-24 defaults the status text to "Draft" when nothing has set one, which is what makes the strip work on a notification that has not been touched yet.

Render the status strip on Origin of the import from the first request, by dropping the committed-answers guard at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:88-89 so the journey always reaches the layout. Nothing blocks it: the reference already exists when the page is first drawn. Starting a notification posts to the backend, which mints the reference and returns the created record, and the user is only then redirected to the origin page under that reference — so the reference is in the page's own URL before a single answer is saved. The guard is a presentation choice, not a symptom of a missing reference. The back-link target on the same page is computed from the same condition and is correct as it stands — a fresh notification's back link goes to the dashboard — so change only the strip, keeping `backLinkFor` on the committed-answers test.

The reference does exist before the first save. `startJourney` calls `records.create()` (src/server/app/engine/journey.js:46-51), the real adapter POSTs to the backend, which mints the reference and returns the created notification (src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/create.js:7-17), and the dashboard's create handler then redirects to the origin page under that id (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/controller.js:115-118). Counts re-derived: 29 of 33 frontend DOMs carry `app-journey-strip` and the four without are the confirmation, the two dashboards and origin, so "the one journey page without it" is exact; 32 of 40 DR1 DOMs carry `app-notification-status`. The default-to-Draft behaviour is at app/views/partials/notification-status.html:3, not at the cited :18-24 — :18-24 is the DR1 branch that renders the strip, which is what the cited range actually shows. increments.title: A private transporter added in DR1 joins the transporter list and can be picked again on the next notification; the frontend keeps it on the one notification it was typed into, so a repeat user retypes the same nine fields every time.
increments.detail:
`/transporters/private` collects the private transporter's name, five address lines, country, telephone number and email address and commits them onto the notification under `privateTransporter` (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/private-transporter-details/private-transporter-details.controller.js). Nothing else reads them. The next notification starts the form blank, and there is nowhere in the service that lists transporters a user has entered before, so a haulier who moves the same animals every week retypes the same record every week.

Saving on DR1's add-private form pushes the transporter onto the user's own transporter records, and the `/transporter` list is built by concatenating those with the eight the service ships (app/routes.js:2903-2905, 3310-3345). The record the user just added is on the list the moment they return to it, alongside the approved ones, with its own Type and Status. Where the add was started from the address book, the same save also copies it into the address book.

Give a transporter somewhere to live other than the notification. That is a persistence change first — a per-organisation transporter collection, or an extension of the address book to carry a transporter's approval number, which the frontend's own note says the address book cannot represent today. Once records survive a notification, the list page shows them and the private form becomes an add-to-the-list step rather than a fill-in-the-blanks step. Ordered after the list page exists; useless before it.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding the frontend writing the private transporter anywhere other than the notification's own answers — an address-book write, a per-organisation collection, or any read of previously entered transporters when the form loads.

increments.title: DR1 hints the arrival date with an example date; the frontend hints it with the two ends of the valid window, so a user reads two dates that are not their answer before reaching the field.
increments.detail:
