increments.title: A DR1 user who cannot find their commercial transporter on the list can add one; a frontend user can only pick from the two the service hands them, and has no way to record a commercial transporter that is not on that list.
increments.detail:
Choosing Commercial leads to `/transporters/select`, which renders the whole commercial list as radios and validates that the answer is one of the ids it rendered (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transporters-select/transporters-select.controller.js:23-29). There is no add link, no manual-entry fallback and no free-text field. Two records exist. If the transporter moving the animals is not one of those two, the notification cannot say who is moving the animals — the journey has no other route through. The private branch does allow free entry, so the only way out today is to misdescribe a commercial transporter as a private one.

DR1's list page has an "Add a transporter" button, and choosing Commercial on the type page reaches `/transporter/add-commercial`, a full create form (app/views/partials/transporter-add-commercial-fields.html). It collects: Transporter authorisation number; Name or organisation name; an address, either through a "Search for an address" lookup or manual entry of Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, County (optional), Postcode or Zip code and Country; and, under an "Enter contact details" heading, Email address and Phone number. The page also repeats the transporter-authorisation guidance in an Important panel so a user filling the form can check the authorisation rules while they do it. Saving adds the transporter to the list and returns the user to it.

Add an add-commercial-transporter page reachable from the transporter list. The whole field set above is new work in the frontend — in particular the transporter authorisation number, which the frontend never collects on either transporter branch. Two decisions sit inside it and both need settling before the page can be built: whether an added commercial transporter is stored on the notification or in a register other notifications can reuse, and whether DR1's Northern-Ireland-only restriction on commercial transporters is a real policy the form must enforce.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding any route in the frontend that records a commercial transporter not present in the commercial-transporter list — an add link, a manual-entry reveal, or a free-text name field on `/transporters/select`.

finding.correction: CLAIMED: DR1 has a full add-commercial-transporter form and the frontend has no way to record a commercial transporter that is not on its list. VERIFIED AGAINST THE PICTURE. The captured dr1-transporter-add-commercial screenshot shows every field the finding enumerates, in order: an Important panel repeating the transporter-authorisation guidance, Transporter authorisation number, Name or organisation name, Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, County (optional), Postcode or Zip code, a disabled Country reading Northern Ireland, then an 'Enter contact details' heading over Email address and Phone number. increments.title: DR1 tells the user a commercial transporter can only be one from Northern Ireland and holds the form to it; the frontend states no such restriction and offers a Swiss and a Belgian commercial transporter to choose from.
increments.detail:
The Commercial radio is hinted "A business approved to transport animals — you will choose one from a list" and says nothing about where the transporter may be based (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:79-82). The list it leads to holds two records: García Livestock Transport SL, in Switzerland, and J & G Campbell LTD, in Belgium (src/server/app/services/commercial-transporters/records.js:7-29). Neither is in Northern Ireland, and nothing in the journey tells a user that where the transporter is based matters.

DR1 asserts the restriction three times over. The Commercial option on the type page is hinted "This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland." (app/data/transporter-types.js:6-10). The add-commercial form's Country select is rendered disabled, showing Northern Ireland, with the real value carried in a hidden field so the user cannot change it (app/views/partials/transporter-add-commercial-fields.html:185-201). And the address lookup on that same form is fed only the Northern Ireland addresses rather than the full set (app/routes.js:3416-3420). It is stated as a rule, not as an example.

Settle first whether the Northern Ireland restriction is a rule about the whole commercial register or only about a transporter a user creates. DR1 answers that question against itself: it states the rule on the add-a-transporter page and then offers Romanian, Irish, Danish and Portuguese commercial transporters on the list behind it. Until that is resolved nothing here is safe to build — adding the hint to the frontend's Commercial radio while the list still holds a Swiss and a Belgian record would reproduce DR1's own contradiction, and deleting those two records would enforce a rule DR1 does not enforce on its own data. What would settle it: the service owner saying whether an approved commercial transporter may be based outside Northern Ireland. If only newly created ones are restricted, this finding is struck and the restriction lives entirely inside transport--cannot-add-a-commercial-transporter, whose form fixes Country to Northern Ireland.

FALSIFIED BY: DR1 offering a commercial transporter based outside Northern Ireland on its own approved list. That observation has already been made — four of the eight records on DR1's transporter list are Commercial and none is Northern Irish — which is why this finding is disputed rather than accepted.

finding.correction: CLAIMED: DR1 restricts commercial transporters to Northern Ireland three ways over, so the frontend must add the hint and purge the Swiss and Belgian records from its commercial list. ALL THREE LEGS TRUE. One: the hint 'This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland.' is in app/data/transporter-types.js:6-10 and is legible in the captured dr1-transporter-add screenshot. Two: the Country select on the add-commercial form is rendered with disabled: true over a hidden input carrying the real value (app/views/partials/transporter-add-commercial-fields.html:185-201), and that value is the constant COMMERCIAL_TRANSPORTER_COUNTRY = 'Northern Ireland' (app/routes.js:2958); the captured dr1-transporter-add-commercial screenshot shows the greyed select reading Northern Ireland. Three: the address lookup on the same form is fed addressBookLookupAddresses.northernIrelandAddresses rather than the full set (app/routes.js:3419). THE ROOT-VIEW LEG IS ALSO TRUE: DR2.1 is mounted under its own /design-release-2.1 prefix with its own view directory (app/routes.js:10992-10996), and the /transporter/add-commercial route renders the bare view name, so app/views/transporter-add-commercial.html and partials/transporter-add-commercial-fields.html are DR1's own files, not a 2.1 addition. FALSE: the inference drawn from those legs. DR1's own approved-transporter register holds four Commercial records and not one is in Northern Ireland — Yusen Logistics (Romania) SRL, Roadtrain Ltd of Dublin, Danish Meat Export ApS of Copenhagen and Portuguese Livestock Lda of Lisbon (app/data/transporters.js), all visible in the captured dr1-transporter screenshot. DR1 therefore does precisely what this finding calls worse than saying nothing: it states the rule on the add page and offers non-Northern-Irish commercial transporters on the list behind it. The restriction governs a transporter a user creates, not the register. So the large half of the difference — deleting records from the frontend's commercial list — is not something DR1 asks for, and the copy half is aimed at the wrong page too, because the frontend's Commercial radio asks which sort of transporter yours is rather than what sort you may add. ONE FINDING OR TWO: neither. The data half is falsified and the copy half has no DR1 counterpart on the paired page. WHAT SURVIVES: DR1 fixes the Country of a newly added commercial transporter to Northern Ireland, which belongs to the add-commercial page the frontend does not have — transport--cannot-add-a-commercial-transporter already names it as a decision inside that page. HOW CHECKED: read app/data/transporter-types.js, app/data/transporters.js, app/views/partials/transporter-add-commercial-fields.html, app/routes.js at 2958, 3395-3430 and 10990-10997; read the captured dr1-transporter, dr1-transporter-add and dr1-transporter-add-commercial screenshots; read src/server/app/services/commercial-transporters/records.js. BAND: frontend-work to disputed.
finding.falsifiedBy: DR1 offering a commercial transporter based outside Northern Ireland on its own approved list. That observation has already been made — four of the eight records on DR1's transporter list are Commercial and none is Northern Irish — which is why this finding is disputed rather than accepted.

increments.detail:
Means of transport to the port of entry is a radios group of four — Airplane, Railway, Road Vehicle, Vessel — occupying about a fifth of the page between the port-of-entry search and the transport identification field (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/port-of-entry/port-of-entry.njk:29-38). increments.title: Two ports appear twice in the frontend's port-of-entry list under different codes — Pembroke Port and Port of Sheerness — so a user picking one has to guess which of two identically named entries is the right one; DR1's list names each port once.
increments.detail:
The port-of-entry search offers seventy-eight ports, and two of them are listed twice. Pembroke Port appears under GB PED and again under GB PEM; Port of Sheerness appears under GBSHS and again under GB SHS, the second of the pair differing only by a space in the code (src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json:182-189, 254-261). Typing "Pembroke" returns two results with identical text, and the user has no way to tell which one the service expects — the codes are the only thing that separates them and nothing on the page explains what a code means. Whichever they pick is stored, so the same physical port arrives at the backend under two different codes depending on which line the user happened to click.

DR1's catalogue names Sheerness once, under GBSHS (app/data/uk-airports.js:175), and has no Pembroke entry at all. It is not free of repeated names, though: eight places appear twice under different codes — Aberdeen, Bristol, Cardiff, Dundee, Glasgow, Inverness, Manchester and Southampton — the airport and the seaport sharing one name. DR1 prints the code after the name, so a user choosing Aberdeen picks between "Aberdeen - ABZ" and "Aberdeen - GBABD" with nothing else to separate them.

Nothing to build until it is settled whether one name under two codes is a defect at all, because DR1 does the same thing eight times over and both services print the code beside the name. What would settle it: the reference-data owner saying whether GB PED and GB PEM are two facilities or one record duplicated. The other pair is worth raising whatever the answer — GBSHS and "GB SHS" are the same five characters with a space gained or lost, which is a data defect on its own terms — but it belongs in a reference-data ticket rather than in this backlog, because DR1 gives no position to compare it against.

FALSIFIED BY: DR1's own port catalogue carrying two entries that share a name and differ only by code. Already observed, on eight names, which is why this finding is disputed rather than accepted.

finding.correction: CLAIMED: the frontend lists Pembroke Port and Port of Sheerness twice while DR1 names every port once. FRONTEND LEG TRUE: the fixture holds GB PED and GB PEM both named 'Pembroke Port' and GBSHS and 'GB SHS' both named 'Port of Sheerness' (src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json:182-189, 253-260), and the captured DOM renders 'Pembroke Port (GB PED)' beside 'Pembroke Port (GB PEM)'. PROTOTYPE LEG FALSE: DR1's catalogue repeats eight names under different codes — Aberdeen (ABZ and GBABD), Bristol, Cardiff, Dundee, Glasgow, Inverness, Manchester (MAN and GBMNC) and Southampton (SOU and GBSOU) — because it lists the airport and the seaport separately. The captured dr1-arrival-details DOM renders 'Aberdeen - ABZ' and 'Aberdeen - GBABD'. DR1 is the oracle and DR1 behaves the same way, so the parity claim does not stand. ALSO OVERSTATED: 'two results with identical text'. Both services append the code, so the option text is not identical — the finding's own next clause concedes the codes separate them. And DR1 has no Pembroke entry of any kind, so it takes no position on that pair. BAND: needs-backend to disputed.

increments.title: Three port names are malformed in the frontend's port-of-entry list — a misspelt Teesport, a shouted TILBURY and a Portsmouth Port with a doubled space — where DR1 spells every port in ordinary sentence case.
increments.detail:
Three of the seventy-eight ports a user can pick are written wrong. GB TEE is named "Teestort", which is not a place — Teesport is (src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json:302-305). GB TIL is named "TILBURY" in capitals, sitting on the same list as "Tilbury Port" and "Tilbury 2 Ro-Ro Terminal" in ordinary case (:294-297). GB PME is named "Portsmouth  Port" with two spaces between the words (:266-269). The misspelling is the one that costs a user something: the search matches on the text as written, so typing "Teesport" returns nothing and the port looks absent from the service.

DR1's catalogue spells two of the same places properly and in ordinary case — Teesport (app/data/uk-airports.js:186) and Tilbury (:189). It has no Portsmouth entry at all, so DR1 takes no position on that third name.

Correct the three names in the reference-data port catalogue: Teestort to Teesport, TILBURY to title case, and the doubled space in Portsmouth Port to one. The codes do not change, so nothing already submitted is affected. The list reaches the frontend from the reference-data service and is only captured into the repo as a fixture, so the correction lands upstream and the fixture is recaptured after it.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding that GB TEE is officially registered as "Teestort" rather than Teesport in the UN/LOCODE data the reference-data service draws on.

ALL THREE FRONTEND DEFECTS CONFIRMED IN THE CAPTURED DOM, not just in source: the port control renders 'Teestort (GB TEE)', 'TILBURY (GB TIL)' and 'Portsmouth  Port (GB PME)' with the doubled space intact (capture/html/frontend/fe-arrival-details.html; fixture at src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json:294-297, 302-305, 266-269). increments.title: DR1 tells a user entering a transporter's phone number to include the country code if it is international; the frontend's phone field carries no hint, on a form whose whole point is that the transporter may be abroad.
increments.detail:
The private transporter form's phone field is labelled Telephone number and has no hint (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/private-transporter-details/private-transporter-details.njk:73-81). The only rule on it is a 20-character maximum. A user entering a transporter based in Ireland, France or anywhere else the consignment starts gets no signal that a bare national number will not be dialable, and the field is on a form that offers a Country select precisely because the transporter is often not in the UK.

DR1 hints the same field "For international numbers include the country code" (app/views/partials/transporter-add-private-fields.html:100-104). It sits under an "Enter contact details" heading with the email address, and the commercial add form carries the identical hint.

Add the hint to the private transporter form's phone field. One line of copy; no validation change is implied and none should be added on the strength of it, because DR1 does not validate the format either. If the add-commercial form is built later it takes the same hint.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a country-code hint on the frontend's transporter phone field — the captured page model lists the field with a null hint.

increments.title: The frontend will not let a user past the transit-countries page until at least one country is ticked; DR1 treats the answer as optional and lets a user continue having named none.
increments.detail:
Once the means of transport is Railway or Road Vehicle the transit-countries page joins the journey, and the page refuses an empty answer: submitting with no box ticked returns the page with "Select at least one country the consignment will travel through" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transit-countries/transit-countries.controller.js:37-39, copy at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:54-55). The obligation model says the same: transitedCountries is in scope and mandatory whenever the means of transport is RAILWAY or ROAD_VEHICLE (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/transport.js:92-104), so the task stays incomplete and the notification cannot be reviewed until a country is named. A consignment moving by road or rail that passes through no third country has nothing true to tick, and the only way past the page is to name a country the animals do not travel through.

DR1 shows the same page under the same rule and never validates it. The POST handler saves whatever list arrived and redirects onward (app/routes.js:10503-10537); there is no error branch for transit countries anywhere in the route file, and the completeness helper is explicit that transit countries are optional and any saved list, including an empty one, is acceptable (app/routes.js:1932-1935). A user who travels through nowhere adds nothing and presses Save and continue.

Make transitedCountries optional while it is in scope: drop the empty-answer error from the page, and change the obligation from mandatory to optional so the hub and the review page stop holding the notification open waiting for an answer. The gate that decides whether the page appears at all does not change — Railway or Road Vehicle, on both sides. Do this with the type-ahead change or after it, since both edit the same page and the two are one visit.

increments.title: DR1 shows each transporter's approval status as a tag — Approved or New — beside its approval number; the frontend shows no status at all, so a user cannot tell an approved transporter from an unapproved one.

Each transporter is one radio, labelled with the name and hinted with the address and approval number joined by an em dash (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:92-93). Nothing on the page says whether the transporter is approved. The page heading calls them "approved commercial transporters", so a user is left to infer that everything on the list is approved — but the underlying records carry no status field to make that true (src/server/app/services/commercial-transporters/records.js:7-29), so the claim is an assumption rather than a fact the service checked.

DR1's table has a Status column, and each row renders a govuk-tag: green Approved for most records, and a pink New for two of the eight (app/views/transporter.html:148-149, app/data/transporters.js). The status sits next to the approval number so a user choosing between two similar records can see which one the service has already approved, and can see when a transporter they added themselves has not been approved yet.

The frontend's commercial list is a hardcoded module the frontend owns, so the field can be added there today and DR1 hardcodes its own statuses the same way — no API has to land first. What does have to be settled is what the two existing records may honestly be labelled, because marking them Approved in the frontend asserts something nothing verified. Ask whoever owns the list, then add the column. When the register moves behind a service the status travels with it.

increments.title: DR1 opens the transporter task on a searchable list of approved transporters and only asks whether one is commercial or private when a user needs to add a record that is not there; the frontend asks the type first and branches the whole journey on the answer.
increments.detail:
The transport task reaches the transporter question at `/transporters`, which asks "What type of transporter will move the animals?" with two radios, Commercial and Private, and hints that describe what happens next — "A business approved to transport animals — you will choose one from a list" and "You or another individual moving the animals — you will give their address" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:78-87). The answer decides the rest of the task: Commercial goes to `/transporters/select`, a radio list of two records, and Private goes to `/transporters/private`, a blank address form. A user who does not know which sort of record theirs is has to guess before seeing anything, and a user whose transporter is already known to the service still starts by answering a classification question. The three pages are ordered type, then list, then form in the section definition (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:67-75).

DR1 opens the task on `/transporter`, which is the record itself: a lead paragraph naming who a transporter is, the transporter-authorisation guidance, then a heading "Select a transporter", a Search field hinted "Name, address or approval number", and a table of eight approved transporters with a radio in the first column and Name, Address, Approval number, Type and Status columns (app/views/transporter.html:73-160). Both commercial and private transporters sit in one table, distinguished by the Type column, so the type is a property of the record shown rather than a question the user answers. Only under the table is there a secondary "Add a transporter" button, and only that button leads to `/transporter/add` — the commercial-or-private question — which opens with the warning "Before you add this transporter, please ensure you have already searched for it first" (app/views/transporter-add.html:31-40). Each row also carries a View details link into the transporter's full record.

Reverse the order of the task. `/transporters` becomes the list page — search over the transporters the service knows about, one row per record showing its type, with a radio to pick one — and the commercial-or-private question moves behind an "Add a transporter" button as the first step of adding a record that is not on the list. The type question keeps its two options but loses the journey-describing hints, because after the move it no longer describes what happens next. Carry the "Before you add this transporter, please ensure you have already searched for it first" warning onto the moved page: it only makes sense once searching comes first. This is the parent of the rest of the transporter findings — the missing search box, the missing approval status, the inability to add a commercial transporter, and the fact that an added transporter is not kept for reuse all land on the list page this creates.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a route in the frontend that reaches a list of transporters without first answering the type question — or finding that DR1 reaches `/transporter/add` from anywhere other than the Add a transporter button on the list.

The previous run reached the same conclusion and retired the objection (carryover inc-064). The frontend's page order is confirmed at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:67-75. TWO THINGS THE DIFFERENCE SHOULD CARRY AND DOES NOT. First, the two type options are ordered and labelled differently: DR1 lists 'Private transporter' then 'Commercial' (app/data/transporter-types.js), the frontend lists 'Commercial' then 'Private' (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:78-87). Too thin for a finding of its own, but it is work on the page this finding moves and it would otherwise be lost. Second, the transporter-authorisation guidance block sits on the frontend's type page and on DR1's list page, so moving the type question moves that block with it.
